en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Earth.
6. The Question on Space “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘five qualities of space should be adopted,’ what are those five qualities that should be adopted?
“Just as space, O Great King, is entirely ungraspable;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must become entirely ungraspable by the defilements.
This, Great King, is the first quality of space that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, space is traversed by hosts of seers, ascetics, spirits, and birds.
In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga, a yogāvacara, should direct the mind toward conditioned phenomena [saṅkhāra] as "impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
This, great king, is the second quality of space that should be adopted.
Furthermore, great king, space is terrifying.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, must cause his mind to be repelled by all rebirths in any state of existence and must not find gratification in them.
This, Great King, is the third quality of space that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, space is infinite, immeasurable, and boundless.
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga must possess infinite virtue and immeasurable knowledge.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of space that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, space is unattached, unclinging, unsupported, and unhindered.

In the same way, Great King, a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, must remain unattached in every respect—to family, to the group, to gain, to dwellings, to impediments, to requisites, and to all defilements;
he must be without clinging, without a fixed footing, and without being obstructed.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of space that should be adopted.
This was also said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the god beyond gods, while instructing his own son Rāhula:
“Just as space, Rāhula, is not established anywhere, even so, Rāhula,
you should develop a meditation equal to space.”
“Rāhula, for one who develops meditation that is equal to space, arisen pleasant and unpleasant contacts will not persist by obsessing the mind.
The sixth inquiry: “Unattached to Space.”
